sources: Luke 15:8 (“Or what woman, if she had ten drachma coins, if she lost one drachma coin, wouldn’t light a lamp, sweep the house, and seek diligently until she found it?”)
Luke 15:9 (“she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found the drachma which I had lost’”)
Luke 15:10 (“there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner repenting”)
Luke 15:1-2 (the setting: grumbling over Jesus eating with sinners), shared with yesterday’s lesson
Luke 15:4, 8, 11 (one sheep of a hundred, one coin of ten, one of two sons), behind the hard question
A drachma was a Greek silver coin close in value to the Roman denarius, a day’s wage (Matthew 20:2)
Captions follow the World English Bible, lightly modernized
check: The why question says the coin was lost inside the house, so someone can be lost close to home (a common preaching link to the elder brother of Luke 15:25-32), not stated in the text. Confirm it is fair.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? have you ever turned your whole home upside down looking for one small thing?
options: me too. then you already know how this story feels.
then you know the relief at the end. listen.
lucky you. this woman wasn’t so lucky. at first.

steps.line: Right after the lost sheep, Jesus told another story. A woman had ten silver coins, each about a day’s pay. Then she lost one.
steps.label: Luke 15:8

steps.q: Her house is small and dark. What do you guess she does?
o: Lets it go; she still has nine
steps.why: Village houses had tiny windows and floors of packed earth. She burns precious lamp oil and sweeps until it turns up.

steps.line: She didn’t wait for morning. She lit a lamp.
steps.label: Luke 15:8

steps.line: She swept the whole house, corner by corner, and searched carefully until she found it.
steps.label: Luke 15:8

steps.q: A sheep can wander off. A coin can’t. What does a lost coin add to the picture?
o: Losing it was her own careless fault
Someone can be lost without walking away
Small things matter less than living ones
steps.why: The coin did nothing to get lost, and it can’t find its way back. Many readers hear this: some people are lost right at home, and the search has to come to them.

steps.line: There it was, in the dust. She held it up in the lamplight.
Then she called her friends and neighbors: “Rejoice with me! I’ve found the coin I lost.”
steps.label: Luke 15:9

steps.pre: Jesus said, “In the same way, there is joy in the presence of the
steps.post: of God over one sinner who turns back.”
steps.why: The angels. Many scholars hear it as a reverent way of saying God himself is glad, without naming him.

steps.q: Jesus told these stories because some people were grumbling. About what?
o: He healed people on the Sabbath
He let women travel with him
He ate with tax collectors and sinners
steps.why: Luke 15 opens with the grumble: “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.” The sheep, the coin and the son are his answer, and each ends in a celebration.

say: here’s what i love. this time the one searching is a woman with a broom. christians read her as a picture of God, just like the shepherd.
and it ends in a party. heaven doesn’t just put up with the lost when they’re found. it celebrates. the third story, the son, you met in week one.

steps.q: One sheep out of a hundred. One coin out of ten. Then one son out of two. What might the three stories be doing?
o: Showing that losses add up over time
Raising the stakes, until the lost one is a son
Saying only the biggest loss really matters
steps.why: Each loss is a bigger share of what you have, until it’s a son. And each story ends in joy.

today.say: throw the party. when someone comes back, to church, to health, to the family, to you, celebrate it out loud today: a message, a meal, a cake. if you’d like, say a one-line thank-you prayer for them: your choice.
options: then do it today. out loud. heaven does.
good. when it happens, don’t keep it quiet.
